routes.description: Establish that contingent existence, a finite cosmic past, life-permitting fine-tuning, objective morality, and the reported resurrection facts form independent but cumulative considerations that are more expected given God than given atheism.
routes.successCriteria: The route succeeds if the cited facts receive adequate support, the theistic explanations fit them better than the principal naturalistic alternatives, and their combined force raises the probability of God's existence under the motion's incremental evidential standard.

motionBridge.description: Show that the cumulative considerations raise the probability of God's existence relative to the relevant background and non-theistic alternatives, without requiring deductive proof or certainty.

centralBridges.description: Establish that contingent reality and a universe with a finite past require an explanation beyond physical spacetime, and connect that necessary transcendent cause to a plausible conception of God.
Establish that life-permitting constants and initial conditions are not adequately explained by necessity, chance, or multiverse selection and are more expected on purposive design.
Establish that objective moral values and duties exist and require an ontological ground supplied by God's necessary moral character rather than by deterministic natural processes.
Establish the relevant historical facts concerning Jesus, show that resurrection explains them better than ordinary rivals, and connect divine vindication of Jesus to evidence for God.

subsidiaryBridges.description: Distinguish absolute nonbeing from quantum vacua, fields, geometries, or other physical states so that physical origin models do not automatically discharge the metaphysical explanatory requirement.
Coordinate the first four considerations as support for generic monotheism and the resurrection consideration as the further bridge from that general conclusion to the God revealed by Jesus.

routes.description: Establish that the affirmative considerations do not constitute adequate evidence for God because their standards and probability assignments lack empirical constraint, naturalistic possibilities remain available, and the historical and moral inferences do not uniquely support a divine explanation.
routes.successCriteria: The route succeeds if the affirmative fails to justify its evidential threshold or to show that God predicts the cited facts better than physical, anthropic, moral-naturalistic, testimonial-error, or unresolved alternatives.

motionBridge.description: Require empirically discriminating, testable, and sufficiently strong support for a supernatural conclusion, and show that informal probability increases or unexplained phenomena do not alone meet that burden.

centralBridges.description: Preserve quantum-gravity, inflationary, eternal-multiverse, brute-fact, or presently unknown physical accounts as alternatives to a supernatural cause of contingent reality or cosmic beginnings.
Explain apparent fine-tuning through dynamical physics and observer selection across varied universes while requiring justified probability measures before inferring purposeful design.

Show that moral behavior and shared judgments can arise through natural and rational processes, and require an account of how divine grounding avoids arbitrariness and conflicting religious interpretation.
Require extraordinary historical support for resurrection and compare the miracle hypothesis with ordinary error, invention, documentary weakness, and other physical explanations.

subsidiaryBridges.description: Limit reliance on classical intuitions about causation, infinity, possibility, and nothingness where empirically informed physical theories permit counterintuitive structures or events.

Distinguish an abstract divine intelligence from specific religious claims and require observations capable of discriminating an unconstrained God hypothesis from incompatible theological alternatives.

sections.title: Evidential Standard and Cumulative Burden
sections.rationale: Covers the motion-level dispute over incremental probability, prior dependence, empirical testability, falsifiability, and the degree of support required for the cumulative considerations to qualify as evidence for God.

sections.title: Contingency, Cosmic Beginning, and Causation
sections.rationale: Covers whether contingent reality and a finite cosmic past require a necessary transcendent cause, alongside brute-fact, quantum-cosmological, multiverse, infinity, and physical-nothing alternatives.

sections.title: Fine-Tuning, Design, and Anthropic Alternatives
sections.rationale: Covers whether life-permitting conditions are more expected under purposive design or can be accounted for through dynamical physics, varied universes, observer selection, and disputes about probability measures.

sections.title: Objective Morality and Divine Grounding
sections.rationale: Covers whether objective moral values and duties require grounding in God's necessary character or can be sustained through natural, rational, and social processes despite determinism and conflicting religious interpretation.

sections.title: Resurrection, Testimony, and Religious Identification
sections.rationale: Covers the historical inference from the reported resurrection facts, the comparative standing of miraculous and ordinary explanations, and the bridge from generic theistic support to specifically Christian claims.

relevanceBurden.rationale: It directly advances the con motion-level adequate-evidence standard while bearing especially on the resurrection claim.
